readings.meaning: Roman numeral five or letter V

ambiguity: Strongly resembles a symmetrical checkmark at small sizes, and functions almost universally as UI chrome (expand/collapse toggle) rather than a task subject icon.

example_tasks.task: Animate the expand chevron smoothly when opening the FAQ rows
Swap the country selector to a native select dropdown on mobile
Bring the winter bins down from the top garage rack
Push daily phone screen time down below two hours this week
Drop the standing desk preset height by two centimeters
Replace the custom JavaScript select menu on the checkout page with a simpler native dropdown
Carry the heavy cast-iron Dutch oven and canning jars down to the cellar shelves
Negotiate the internet bill down to the promotional rate before the twelve-month contract renews

reasoning: This is a standard downward chevron used as UI chrome for expanding accordions or opening dropdown menus. In a to-do list, users will read it as an interface control to expand subtasks or mistake it for a completion checkmark, making it unsuitable as a topical task icon.
